g12-physics-up4-t1.overview: Magnetism is a force that acts at a distance through an invisible field: lodestones, compasses and every electric motor start here. Permanent magnets, domains, poles and the Earth's own magnetism form the foundation the current-magnetism topics build on.
objectives: Describe magnetic materials and the pole law (like repel, unlike attract)
Explain magnetisation by domains and Curie temperature
Distinguish hard and soft magnetic materials
Use a compass to detect fields
Explain Earth's magnetism and magnetic declination
g12-physics-up4-t1.simple: Invisible bars of force. A magnet drags iron because its atomic current loops — electron spins — stand in army rows (domains). Break a magnet and every piece still has both poles: monopoles never show up. The Earth itself is a giant, its molten iron interior generating the field your phone's compass reads — pointing roughly north, off by the local declination.
g12-physics-up4-t1.detailed:
Poles and the pole law. Every magnet has a north and south seeking pole: suspended, it aligns N-to-geographic-north (which is therefore a magnetic SOUTH pole — the naming is historical). Like poles repel, unlike attract. Force follows an inverse-square-like law at distance (dipole fields fall faster, ∝ 1/r⁴ for the force gradient) and is strongest at the poles, where field lines crowd.

Domains. In iron, cobalt, nickel and steel, billions of atomic magnetic moments lock into parallel within micrometre-scale domains. Unmagnetised iron: domains cancel. Magnetising (stroking, coil field, hammering in a field) grows aligned domains. Heat past the Curie point (iron 770 °C) and thermal chaos scrambles them — a red-hot magnet dies. Drop one and it partly demagnetises: mechanical shock unseats walls.

Hard vs soft. Soft iron: domains move easily — strong but temporary magnets (electromagnet cores, transformer laminations, relay poles). Hard steel and modern alloys (Alnico, NdFeB, ferrite): domains lock — permanent speakers, fridge magnets, compass needles. NdFeB grades lift 1 kg on their own weight from a coin-sized disc; keep them away from drives and pacemakers.

Earth's field. Generated by convection of molten iron-nickel in the outer core (geodynamo): tilted ~11° from the rotation axis and wandering — Addis Ababa's compass declination is a couple of degrees west and drifting. Field strength at the surface ~25–65 µT (half a gauss). The tilt and dips (inclination) point toward the magnetic poles; compasses flatten for navigation use. The poles even flip every few hundred thousand years — recorded in seafloor basalt stripes.

Detection & uses. Iron filings reveal patterns; a compass surveys direction; Hall probes measure strength electronically — the same sensor in brushless motors and phone cover switches. Magnet therapy claims aside, medicine uses real magnetism: MRI (Unit 1.3) and magnetic drug targeting research.

workedExamples.calculation: Magnetic north lies 3° west of true: every magnetic reading runs 3° high, so true = magnetic − 3°.
workedExamples.answer: 087° true.

workedExamples.answer: 8× weaker — magnets are short-range power.

Speakers and mics: permanent magnet + voice coil
Electricity generation: all turbines spin coils in magnet fields
Magnetic separators in flour milling and mining
g12-physics-up4-t1.summary: Domains align, poles pair, Earth dynamos: magnetism is dipole-field physics — strong close, gone fast, never cut into monopoles.

g12-physics-up4-t2.overview: Field lines turn invisible magnetism into a map: their direction shows where a north pole would be pushed, their density shows how hard. This topic builds the line-drawing fluency — bar, Earth, and the right-hand rules that connect currents to their circular fields.
objectives: Draw and interpret magnetic field line patterns
State field-line rules (N→S outside, no crossings, density = strength)
Use right-hand grip rules for wires, coils and solenoids
Predict field direction at any point between magnets
Sketch the uniform field between pole pieces
g12-physics-up4-t2.simple: Arrows you can trust. Trace a compass around a bar magnet: it always points along an imaginary line — draw them and you have the field map. Lines leave the north pole, enter the south, never cross, crowd where the field is strong. Around a current-carrying wire they form circles: thumb with the current, fingers curl with the field. Right hand, always.
g12-physics-up4-t2.detailed:
The convention. A field line's tangent gives the force direction on a north pole placed there (equivalently, a compass needle's N end). Outside a magnet: N→S; inside: S→N (lines are CLOSED loops — this is why no monopoles: no start, no end). Iron filings align along them; the density of lines (flux per area, B in tesla) encodes strength. Two like poles: lines avoid, showing the neutral point where fields cancel. Opposite poles: lines bridge — attraction mapped.

Uniform fields. Between large flat opposite poles (shoe-magnet gaps, moving-coil meter magnets) lines are parallel and equally spaced: constant strength and direction. That is why meter coils get curved poles with a soft-iron cylinder: radial uniform magnitude everywhere the coil turns.

Currents make circular fields. Straight wire: concentric circles, sense by right-hand grip (thumb = conventional current, fingers = B). Magnitude B = µ₀I/2πr — doubles current, doubles field; doubles distance, halves it. Earth's own field (~50 µT) is the classroom's first rival: place wires north-south to see compasses swing (Oersted's 1820 discovery that launched electromagnetism).

Coils and solenoids. Each loop's circular field adds inside the coil: a solenoid mimics a bar magnet, N determined by the grip (curl fingers with current, thumb points to the solenoid's N). Field inside: B ∝ µ₀ n I (n = turns/length) — uniform and strong in the core, adding a soft-iron core multiplies it. Loops stacked = the design of every electromagnet, relay and MRI bore.

Drawing exam skills. Mark arrows N→S outside; never cross lines; crowd near poles; show the neutral point on the axis between like poles. For wire+external-field superposition (motor effect next topic), remember fields add vectorially — the 'catapult field' picture of a wire's circles riding on a uniform field.

g12-physics-up4-t3.overview: When a current-carrying conductor sits in an external magnetic field, it feels a force — the motor effect — and this single phenomenon drives every electric motor, loudspeaker, relay and moving-coil meter, and defines the tesla itself.
objectives: Apply F = BIL sinθ with Fleming's left-hand rule
Explain the catapult-field picture of the force
Describe loudspeaker and moving-coil meter operation
Explain DC motor commutation and rotation
Use F = BQv for charged beams
g12-physics-up4-t3.simple: Two fields fight; the wire gets shoved. The wire's circular field rides on the magnet's uniform field: denser on one side, thinner on the other, and the wire is pushed from crowded toward sparse — like a compressed spring releasing. Fleming's left hand indexes it: First = Force, Field, current. Reverse current, reverse force. That shove, looped round a coil and switched at the right moment, is a motor.
g12-physics-up4-t3.detailed:
The force law. F = BIL sinθ: length L of wire carrying I in field B, θ between wire and field. Maximum when perpendicular (sin 90° = 1), zero when parallel — a wire laid along the field feels nothing. 1 T × 1 m × 1 A = 1 N: the tesla's definition lives in this push. Direction: Fleming's LEFT hand (motor), index = field (N→S), middle = conventional current, thumb = force/motion. Reserve right hand for generators/grips — the pair is tradition's trap; sort them by 'MOTor uses left (motor needs Fleming L), GENerator uses right'.

Catapult field. Superpose the wire's circles with the external field: reinforcement below, cancellation above ⇒ a gradient of magnetic 'pressure' pushing the wire from strong to weak side. The picture earns the name: the field is stretched like a bowstring that wants to straighten.

Loudspeaker. Audio current through a voice coil suspended in a radial magnet gap: F = BIL with I following the music — the coil (glued to the cone) shoves back and forth, air follows, sound. Reversed polarity across two speakers cancels bass (out of phase); damping comes from the coil's own back-EMF (next topics close the loop).

DC motor. Coil in a field: forces on the two sides are equal/opposite — a couple, torque τ = NIAB sinθ. The split-ring commutator flips current every half-turn so the couple keeps its sense: rotation. Brushless motors do the switching electronically. Motors also generate when spun (regenerative braking in EVs) — the same law run backward.

Moving-coil meter. Coil on pivots in a radial field with hairsprings: torque NIAB meets spring restoring torque kθ — pointer reads current linearly. Curved poles + soft core keep B radial so the scale is uniform. Galvanometers become ammeters with shunts and voltmeters with multipliers.

Charged particles. F = BQv sinθ, velocity-perpendicular version; the force is always ⊥ motion ⇒ circular paths, r = mv/BQ — mass spectrometers, cyclotrons, and the aurora as Earth's field steering solar electrons into the poles.

g12-physics-up4-t4.overview: Push a magnet into a coil and current appears — electromagnetic induction, the bridge from motion to electricity discovered by Faraday (and Henry) in 1831. Changing magnetic flux induces EMF; Lenz's law fixes its direction. It runs every generator on Earth.
objectives: Explain induced EMF from changing flux
State and apply Lenz's law (opposition, energy conservation)
Describe generator action and slip rings/commutators
Explain back-EMF in motors
List ways to increase induced EMF
g12-physics-up4-t4.simple: Electricity by wiggling magnetism. Stationary magnet in a coil: nothing. MOVE it and the needle kicks — the changing flux shakes electrons along. Push the magnet in and the induced current resists your push; pull and it resists the pull (Lenz) — the electrical energy you harvest is the mechanical work you did. Every power station does this at scale: turbine spins coil, coil resists, grid receives.
g12-physics-up4-t4.detailed:
Flux and the induction condition. Φ = BA cosθ through a loop. Induction needs CHANGE: move the magnet, vary the current in a neighbour, spin the coil, or deform the circuit. EMF appears ONLY while flux changes — a held magnet gives zero despite strong field. Faster change ⇒ bigger EMF; more turns multiply it (each loop's EMF adds).

Lenz's law. The induced current flows so its OWN field opposes the change that made it. Push N-pole into a coil face: the face becomes N to repel you — you feel resistance, and your work becomes the coil's energy. Pull it out: the face turns S and pulls back — again opposing. Energy conservation in circuit language; 'opposes the CHANGE', not the flux itself.

Generators. Rotate a coil in a field: θ(t) changes ⇒ flux swings sinusoidally ⇒ EMF ∝ NBAω sinωt — alternating, at the spin frequency. Slip rings feed AC to the grid (Ethiopian power: 50 Hz from turbine rotation). A split-ring commutator instead rectifies the output to pulsing DC. EMF peaks by field strength, coil area, turns and speed — hence hydro turbines at Gibe spinning huge slow coils through enormous magnet flux.

Back-EMF. A motor is also a generator: its spinning coil cuts flux and induces an EMF opposing the supply. At switch-on the coil is still ⇒ back-EMF zero ⇒ inrush current huge (motors need starters; large ones burn fuses otherwise). At speed, back-EMF grows until net drive = IR small. Stall a running drill: it slows, back-EMF drops, current spikes, it heats — the failure mode of every motor.

Dynamic EMF (motional). A conductor of length L moving at v across B: F = BQv separates charges until EQ = BQv ⇒ ε = BLv. Rails and a sliding bar, a bicycle dynamo, and the 3 kV/m induced across jet wings at 250 m/s all live here — the wire version of Faraday.

g12-physics-up4-t5.overview: Faraday put induction's size into an equation: induced EMF equals the rate of flux linkage change. Combined with Lenz's direction rule, ε = −N ΔΦ/Δt quantifies every generator, predicts transformer voltages and explains why spinning faster or winding tighter earns more volts.
objectives: Define flux linkage NΦ and state Faraday's law
Compute EMF from rates of flux change
Interpret the minus sign as Lenz's law
Derive the transformer ratio from Faraday
Describe flux-change graphs and AC EMF shape
g12-physics-up4-t5.simple: How fast, how much. Lenz says which way; Faraday says how big: volts = turns × how fast the flux through each turn changes. Yank a magnet in over 0.1 s: 10× the EMF of a 1 s push. Double the turns: double the volts. Write it once — ε = −N ΔΦ/Δt — and generators, transformers and induction cooktops all read off the same line.
g12-physics-up4-t5.detailed:
Flux linkage. One loop feels Φ = BA cosθ; N loops in series link NΦ (weber-turns). Faraday's experiments (1831): the induced EMF is proportional to d(NΦ)/dt — the CHANGE RATE, not the change itself. Same ΔΦ in half the time: twice the volts. Stop the change: zero EMF even with huge flux present.

The minus sign. ε = −d(NΦ)/dt encodes Lenz: the induced EMF drives currents whose effect opposes the flux change causing it. Drop the magnet down a copper pipe and it falls in slow motion: circulating eddy currents oppose its every gain of speed — kinetic energy quietly converted to pipe heat. The terminal velocity it reaches is the point where magnetic drag equals weight; the energy balance is exactly a generator braking itself.

AC shape. Rotate a coil: Φ = BA cosωt ⇒ ε = NBAω sinωt — sinusoidal EMF, peak ε₀ = NBAω, RMS ε₀/√2 (mains 230 V RMS = 325 V peak). Frequency of the sine = rotation frequency. Ethiopian and European 50 Hz mains: turbines turn coils at 50 rev/s (2 poles) or mechanical fractions with more pole pairs.

Transformer derivation. Primary and secondary share one iron core, hence one Φ(t) through both. Faraday on each: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p exactly — voltage scales with turns. Power conservation (ideal) then forces I_s/I_p = N_p/N_s: step-up voltage steps-down current, which is why the grid transmits at hundreds of kV (loss = I²R shrinks with the current).

Experiment patterns. Plot induced EMF vs magnet speed: linear through origin. vs coil turns: linear. A flux-vs-time square wave gives EMF spikes at the edges (rate of change: infinite at ideal steps); a sine flux gives cosine EMF — always 90° ahead. These graph signatures are exam favorites.

g12-physics-up4-t6.overview: The transformer moves AC power between voltages with no moving parts, at 95–99 % efficiency. Two coils on one iron core, one turns ratio: step up for long-distance transmission, step down for the socket — the reason a national grid at all is possible.
objectives: Describe the core-and-coils construction and working
Apply V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p and the ideal power relation
Explain why transformers need AC, not DC
List real losses (resistive, eddy, hysteresis, flux leakage) and fixes
Trace the Ethiopian transmission chain: plant → 400 kV → 15 kV → 230 V
g12-physics-up4-t6.simple: AC's gearbox. Alternating current in the primary makes an alternating flux in the iron core; Faraday gives the secondary turns the same flux, hence voltage scaled by the turns ratio. Double the turns, double the volts, halve the amps — energy untouched. Step it up to 400 kV, send it 800 km from the Gibe dams, step it down street by street to your socket.
g12-physics-up4-t6.detailed:
Working. Soft-iron core channels nearly all primary flux through the secondary. AC primary current ⇒ alternating Φ ⇒ EMFs in both windings ∝ their turns: V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p. Step-up (N_s > N_p): voltage rises, current falls (ideal: V_p I_p = V_s I_s). Step-down does the mirror. No AC? No changing flux? No induced voltage: an ideal transformer on DC outputs only a transient at switch-on/off. That's why the whole world standardized AC grids (with electronics converting back for batteries and DC links).

Why high voltage at all. Line loss = I²R. For fixed power P = VI, ×10 the voltage ⇒ ÷10 the current ⇒ ÷100 the loss. Ethiopian Transmission Company runs 400 kV and 230 kV lines precisely so the southern hydro and northern plants can trade power with small waste. Local substations step 230/15 kV; pole transformers finish at 230 V.

Losses and their cures. (1) Winding resistance I²R: thick copper, cooling. (2) Eddy currents circulating in the core: laminated sheets (insulated layers) chop the loops. (3) Hysteresis:Domains flip-flopping heats the core — soft iron with a narrow B-H loop minimises it. (4) Flux leakage: imperfect coupling — toroidal cores and close winding keep flux inside. Together: real transformers run 95–99 % efficient; humming pole cans are warm for these same four reasons.

Isolation and safety. No wire joins primary and secondary — only magnetism crosses. This galvanic isolation is why transformers protect: the 230 V side can float free of earth, and faults get contained. Old radio sets and modern medical devices both exploit it. Current transformers (CTs) for metering run near short-circuit; potential transformers (VTs) near open — the wrong one of each gets dangerous fast (VT/CT polarity is a lineman's caution point).

Worked numerics to own. Ratios with currents and power; losses P_line = I²R before/after stepping; the classic 'why not transmit at 230 V?' (answer: 1 740 A for 400 kW — copper the size of tree trunks).

g12-physics-up4-t7.overview: Electromagnetism leaves the textbook here: induction loop security gates, maglev trains, MRI safety, EMI shielding and the practical ethics of an electrified world. This topic connects Unit 4's laws to devices and public safety.
objectives: Explain eddy-current devices: braking, detection, heating
Describe induction-loop and transformer-based systems
Summarise maglev lift/propulsion physics
State MRI and electromagnetic-safety practice
Explain EMI causes and shielding methods
g12-physics-up4-t7.simple: From laws to lives. A train's copper fins over magnets brake without touching wheels (Lenz drag). A shop gate reads a tag as a moving transformer (induction). A maglev floats on repelling fields and never touches rail. MRI scanners run at 6 000 Earths and turn pacemakers into missiles. Same four equations — the difference is scale and safety culture.
g12-physics-up4-t7.detailed:
Eddy-current applications. Trains and roller coasters: magnets sweeping conductive rails induce circulating currents whose fields oppose the motion — speed-proportional braking, frictionless and fade-proof at high speed but weak when slow (disc pads handle stops). Induction cooktops: 20–100 kHz coil drives eddy currents in ferromagnetic pans — the pan heats, the glass stays cool-ish. Metal detectors and airport gates: an AC probe field; metal disturbs it with its own eddy currents — pickup coils notice. Mine-scale conveyor separation and coin sorting use the same trick.

Maglev. Electromagnets (or superconducting coils) levitate the car 1–10 cm above the guideway: no wheel contact ⇒ no rolling friction, less noise, 400–600 km/h (Shanghai line tops service at 430 km/h). Propulsion is a linear synchronous motor: the guideway's travelling magnetic field drags the train's onboard magnets forward. Japan's SCMaglev hit 603 km/h in tests; Lenz's law provides the passive stability in the repulsion design.

MRI and biomedical fields. 1.5–3 T steady fields (30 000–60 000× Earth) plus rapid switching gradients. Danger ladder: ferromagnetic objects fly to the bore (the 'missile effect'); pacemaker and implant wires can heat or malfunction; peripheral-nerve stimulation at high dB/dt. Zones I–IV control access; screening is physics-enforced. The RF pulses are non-ionising — unlike X-rays, no DNA damage, which is why MRI scans pregnant patients when needed.

EMI and shielding. Any switched current radiates; any loop catches. Phone-to-speaker buzz, ignition interference, motor spikes resetting computers — all Faraday coupling. Cures: twisted pairs (loops cancel), coax and mu-metal (field diverted/shorted), Faraday cages (enclosing conductor drains fields), filtering (ferrites choke high-frequency paths), and standards (Ethiopian/European EMC rules cap emissions). Grounding is the safe-return discipline: earth the cage, never the signal loop — ground loops themselves hum.

Reading a power-quality plate. Transformer nameplates, cable ratings, fuses: the physics of Unit 4 all becomes label-reading. When the Addis grid brown-outs, induction motors stall and draw locked-rotor current — which trips protection, for exactly the back-EMF reason from topic 4.

workedExamples.problem: Induction cooktop vs ceramic pan: why no heat?
workedExamples.calculation: Ceramic: no mobile charges ⇒ no eddy currents; ferromagnetic pans also concentrate flux.
workedExamples.answer: Coupling needs conductivity (and permeability helps).

workedExamples.problem: Maglev levitation power vs train power: why is suspension cheaper at speed?
workedExamples.calculation: No wheel-rail contact losses; drag is air only (grows v² but the magnets do no frictional work).
workedExamples.answer: The energy saving is friction, not the magnets.

workedExamples.problem: A shielded cable still hums: ground loop.
workedExamples.calculation: Two earth points at different potentials + the shield = a big loop catching 50 Hz.
workedExamples.answer: Bond the shield at ONE end: break the loop, keep the shield.

workedExamples.problem: Pacemaker near MRI: what fails?
workedExamples.calculation: Static field torques/immobilises reed switches; gradients induce mA-level currents in leads (heating).
workedExamples.answer: MRI-conditional models and protocols exist — otherwise: absolute NO.

commonMistakes: Expecting eddy brakes to hold a parked vehicle (force ∝ speed: zero at standstill)
Thinking maglev magnets 'create energy' (lift costs; propulsion still from the grid)
MRI zone 4 = 'metal detector check' (screening is stricter: ferromagnetic = banned)
Shielding by grounding BOTH ends (creates the loop you tried to kill)
Assuming all 'EMF radiation' is ionising like X-rays (it isn't below UV)
